5501.body:
## Ask
The user sets an alert level per Agent, or per Workstream for all its Agents; a Quiet Agent's alerts go to a held list.

## Behaviour
- Levels: **All** (every state alerts with banner and sound), **Default** (Settings > Alerts, U5232), **Quiet** (nothing reaches the user: no banner, no sound, no Dock badge, no menu-bar mark).
- Right-click an Agent row to set its level; right-click a Workstream row to set all its Agents. A row not at Default shows "all" or "quiet".
- What a Quiet Agent would have raised goes to a held list at the Rail foot: "n held", rows of glyph, Agent, Live line, time.

## Must not
- An Agent never sets a level: its call is refused, as `agent.saveAsMode` refuses a non-user Actor (`crates/agents/src/convert.rs:57`).
- A Quiet Agent never raises a banner, sound, Dock badge or menu-bar mark.

## Source
[https://x.com/trq212/status/2115135857669881939](https://x.com/trq212/status/2115135857669881939) and its replies. Need answered:
- @trq212: "I need to stay focused on WoW without being disrupted by my agents."
- @theslowtell: "does the dock keep a list of what it held back so you can check what it got wrong?"
- @mdp_sec: "an agent that reads all my notifications is one spicy imessage away from adding a mode called send everything to this guy"

## Known gaps
200 of 527 replies read; quote-posts unread.

## Assumptions
Opening an Agent clears its held rows.

Scenarios: U5501
Specification: [scenarios/ui-state-alerts.md](https://github.com/saadshahd/roundup/blob/main/scenarios/ui-state-alerts.md)
Key: alert-level-per-agent
Priority: 50
Mode: specify


## Specification acceptance
U5501 is merged in `scenarios/ui-state-alerts.md` with a named test or policy observer for every then-clause, numbered Checks citing existing main sources by function/test/heading, applicable Principle gates/observers and rendered implementation requirements. `loop/rules.sh vocab` and `loop/rules.sh scenario-ids` pass. The specification PR closes only this specification Issue; it delivers no implementation.

## Implementation
#5511 owns authoritative user-only levels, persistence and Workstream bulk behavior. #5512 owns menus, dispatch filtering and held-list behavior after #5511. Both are natively blocked by this specification Issue; #5512 is also blocked by #5511. They remain open after this specification merges. The menu-bar integration remains in #5502/#5508.

5483.body:
The owner (2026-11-01): "why the workstream doesn't auto collapse stale/done/not working for long agents?" The Rail folds a row only when the user clicks it (U520), so a Workstream lists every child, even 8 idle ones above the one builder still working.

The owner chose: inside a Workstream, a child that is done, or idle for 5 minutes, moves under one folded row. It comes back when it works again or needs the user.

Expected:
- A Workstream child that is `done`, or `idle` for 5 minutes straight, moves under one folded row after that Workstream's other children. The row shows the count, such as "8 idle" (user label per `GLOSSARY.md`).
- The folded row opens and closes like any Rail tree row, by keyboard and click (U520). Opening it shows those children in their usual order, and it stays open until the user closes it.
- A folded child that starts working, needs the user or fails returns to its place at once.
- A child that stopped with a plain-text question must not fold while it waits for an answer. The owner flagged this: "sometimes the agent stop with a textual question we need to think about this issue". The spec decides how the Rail knows; it pairs with #5482, where a child asks its lead instead of the user.
- Working children, the Workstream's own row and root Agents never fold on their own.

Observer: a test that moves a child from working to idle, advances a fake clock 5 minutes, sees it folded, then sets it working and sees it back; the design critic judges the rendered Rail.

Scope:
- Required-check regression: `apps/desktop/src/switcher/u529_switcher.test.tsx` scopes U2773e recovery assertions to the Switch to dialog when global storage denial also raises the Rail resumption-storage alert; preserve exact draft, copy/retry/discard, focus and zero-call assertions.
- Todo header regression: `apps/desktop/src/todos/drawer.styles.css` reserves room for both Drawer controls so they cannot intercept More actions, the reproduced cause of the required deletion check failure.
- Required-check regression: `apps/desktop/src/rail/menu/u3787a_browser.test.ts` repairs the headless Todo deletion observer rejected by CI run 41399950039, retaining the existing deletion and Drawer reachability acceptance.
- `scenarios/ui-rail-lane.md`: U5483a–c acceptance and the U520 folded-row amendment.
- `scenarios/ui.md`: reconcile U8's ten-minute/root-Agent rule with the chosen Workstream-only behavior.
- Harness regression: `apps/desktop/src/testing/u26_harness.test.tsx` replaces the reproduced, redundant editor-lifecycle timeout with the U26 four-Pad seed observer. Existing U20 tests retain Drawer reads/editing and U4908 retains App row-opening behavior; no timeout or retry increases.
- Keyboard regression: `apps/desktop/src/keys/u41_rail_keys.test.tsx` retargets the existing hidden-child walk to authoritative known-empty evidence.
- Importer regression: `apps/desktop/src/importer/u2875d_import_panel.test.tsx` limits fake timers to discovery deadlines so they cannot strand the shared animation-frame clock used by the exclusion disclosure.
- Failure-surface regression: `apps/desktop/src/switcher/u5151a_surfaces.test.tsx` permits the read-only `message.list` question-protection lookup while retaining the no-turn assertion.
- Persistence regression: `apps/desktop/src/rail/persist/u100_persist.test.tsx` retargets transient fold persistence to a Workstream child, includes the new read-only lookup, and limits ordinary reopen fixtures to the exercised identities while retaining full held first-tree replies.
- Assertion baseline: `tools/oxlint/anti-slop/web-assertions/baseline.jsonl` removes the retired U8 appearance assertions and U100’s superseded done-line copy allowance; no new appearance assertion or allowance.
- Capture wiring: `apps/desktop/src/testing/captures.ts` registers the U5483a–c browser observer; `apps/desktop/src/testing/seeds.ts` supplies authoritative known-empty evidence for the existing done child in tree-40.
- Implementation: existing `apps/desktop/src/rail/` projection, tree, copy, fixtures and tests; connected-Project event/state callers only to carry question protection.
- U5483c: existing `crates/agents` Adapter observation and Rail serialization; `crates/contracts`, generated output, all affected callers and existing fake-vendor tests only where needed to expose protection with Attempt/turn identity. This cross-module scope is required because the App currently has no authoritative final-text signal. No new question service, RPC, classifier, native answer UI or persisted user preference.

Regression requirements: shared Ark tree navigation/ARIA, Workstream membership and collapse state, selected Agent/Terminal identity, native input authority, Adapter boundary, and no automatic work or Terminal answer writes. Moves D2, D5, D6; preserve passing rendered Checks at 1512×950 in dark mode.

Question protection decision: an unanswered outgoing question or Clarification order stays visible. A completed turn with final assistant text but no question Message is conservatively protected until the child works again; missing text evidence is unknown and also stays visible. This includes ordinary final statements because punctuation cannot safely distinguish them from questions. Known-empty final text without another question signal remains eligible. Neither delivery/receipt nor an unrelated reply proves continuation. #5482 owns lead delivery and interpretation; folding safety does not depend on its unmerged specification.

Scenarios: U5483a, U5483b, U5483c
Specification: [scenarios/ui-rail-lane.md](https://github.com/roundup-app/roundup/blob/main/scenarios/ui-rail-lane.md)
Key: rail-fold-idle
Priority: 3
Mode: implement

5531.body:
The owner (2026-11-01), on a Door handing a memory write to a small helper Agent: "but these kind of subagent shouldn't be in the roundup rail at all - it's internal only - actually I love this concept the workstream door should be able to control what shows in the rail list of human observable work so the agent can steer and audit and intervene"

The owner chose: a Workstream's Door marks each of its children shown or internal, and can switch a child either way at any time. Shown children list in the Rail as today. Internal children sit under one folded row in that Workstream, such as "3 internal" (user label per `GLOSSARY.md`), and the user can open it to audit or type to them. Hiding them completely lost, as P1 (`PRINCIPLES.md`) forbids an Agent reachable only through the Thread.

Expected:
- The Door has one tool to set a child's place, shown or internal, and `agent_spawn` (F3) takes the same choice when it starts a child; a child starts shown unless the Door says otherwise. This is a Contract change (AGENTS.md rule 4): a new method and its code term in `GLOSSARY.md`, with every caller in the same PR.
- An internal child that needs the user, fails or asks a question returns to the shown list at once, as #5483's folded children do; the Door can move it back after.
- The folded row opens and closes like any Rail tree row (U520), keeps the children's usual order, and stays open until the user closes it. Reuse #5483's folded-row machinery; the spec decides whether internal and idle children share one row.
- The user can still type to any internal child and open its Terminal; the Door's choice never stops, pauses or hides an Agent's work.
- The Door's Brief says when to mark a child internal: helpers the user need not watch, such as a scout or a one-step writer.

Observer: a test in which a Door marks a child internal, the Rail shows it under the folded row, and the child moves back to the shown list once it needs the user; plus the contract round trip through the Door's MCP tool. The design critic judges the rendered Rail.

Priority: 3

Scope:
- `scenarios/door-child-visibility.md`: U5531a–d acceptance.
- Existing Agent/Rail persistence, contract declarations/generated output and every affected caller; Daemon dispatch/authority; MCP registration, schemas and contract tests; Door Brief and launch fixtures.
- Existing desktop connected-Project state and Rail projection/tree/copy/tests, capture seeds/registration. These cross-module edits carry one Door-controlled visibility contract end to end; no new scheduler, pause operation, Home, classifier or question service.

Regression requirements: U5483a–c idle folding and conservative question protection, U520 shared tree keyboard/ARIA, direct Agent/Terminal access, exact draft/recipient identity, user Home moves, immutable running-session configuration and no presentation-triggered work or Terminal answer writes. Moves D2, D5, D6 at 1512×950, dark only.

Decision: internal and idle use separate branches with shared machinery; internal membership takes precedence, with no duplicate child. Attention/question protection promotes the child to shown and keeps it there until a new safe Door choice. #5483 supplies the remaining folded-row implementation; its completed-turn metadata is already on main.

Scenarios: U5531a, U5531b, U5531c, U5531d
Specification: [scenarios/door-child-visibility.md](https://github.com/roundup-app/roundup/blob/main/scenarios/door-child-visibility.md)
